scenario: A trap raised during matching -- in a single-pattern `where` test, before any activation exists -- carries the node-derived rule name `$beta_<id>` (LERR.9.11), on the fault fact's `rule` slot (LERR.9.2). The `where` divides, so it is a join test on the pattern's beta and not an alpha test (IRET.6.4: an alpha test compares a slot with a literal and cannot trap) -- the site LERR.1.4.3.not_type_or_engine_error pins. Int slots, because an Int division by zero traps and a Float one is IEEE. The handler matches the name with a regex, since the id is compiler-assigned and not written in the vector. Then the fault-fact queue at the end of propagation (LERR.9.7). Pin: assert S(a=1, b=0); pump. Messages are ['DIVIDE_BY_ZERO beta']; `div` never fires. A runtime that wrote the rule `div`, an empty name, `$engine`, an `$alpha_` name, or a `__beta_<id>__` spelling fails the regex and logs nothing. The `$` is escaped in the regex, where it would otherwise anchor the end.
rules_ds:
schema S scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    a: Int mutable
    b: Int mutable

rule div:
    S s where s.a / s.b > 1
->
    log critical "fired"

rule handler:
    ComputationError e where e.rule ~ /^\$beta_[0-9]+$/
->
    log critical "{e.kind} beta"
